terms_of_business: All of the coins for sale in this catalogue are guaranteed to be genuine and as described. Orders with accompanying payments are preferred, and postage will not be charged to all orders over $100.00 (add $1.00 for postage and handling on orders less than $100.00). All approval orders will be charged exact postage and insurance costs. All orders may be returned within seven (7) days of arrival if not entirely satisfactory. All goods delivered within the state of California are subject to the 6 percent sales tax. Foreign residents please render payment in U.S. dollars (check drawn on a U.S. bank).
As most coins are one of a kind, a list of alternate choices is recommended.

listings.description: The Catuvellauni, Cunobelin, 10-40 A.D., debased AV stater (5.34 gm). Camulodunum mint. CA—MV, corn ear/Horse prancing right, branch above, CVNO below, two pellets in field. Mack, The Coinage of Ancient Britian, 203. The warlike tribe of the Catuvellauni occupied a portion of Southern England, and Caesar wrote about the tribe in his commentaries, describing the stiff resistance offered by king Cassivellaunus in 54 B.C. Cunobelin, known from Roman literary sources, was a powerful king who extended the area of Catuvellaunian dominion. His son and heir Caratacus led the resistance to Claudius.
Sicily, Agrigentum, fifth century B.C., AR litra (0.71 gm). A[K]—RA, eagle standing left on Ionic capital/Crab, ΛI retrograde below. SNG Copenhagen 49.
Sicily, Agrigentum, 279-241 B.C., AR drachm (3.47 gm). Laureate head of Zeus right/AKPAΓ—AN TIN—W—N, eagle standing right with wings spread, A in right field. SNG Copenhagen 105.

Sicily, Naxos, 550-530 B.C., AR litra (0.65 gm). Bearded head of Dionysus left, crowned with ivy, border of dots between concentric circles/NA—XION retrograde, grape cluster, border of dots between concentric circles. Cahn, The Coins of the Sicilian City of Naxos, 14 (V9/R13).
Sicily, Selinus, circa 440 B.C., AE trias (9.85 gm). Head of nymph left/Selinon leaf, three pellets. Gabrici pl. i, 14.
Sicily, Syracuse, after 480 B.C., AR litra (0.60 gm). Barbarous issue. Head of Arethusa right/Four-spoked wheel. Boehringer B46.

Sicily, Syracuse, circa 470-465 B.C., AR tetradrachm (17.07 gm). Slow quadriga right driven by bearded charioteer, Nike flying right to crown horses/ΣVRAKOΣION, head of Arethusa right surrounded by four dolphins. Boehringer 293 (V139/R201).

Sicily, Syracuse, circa 465-460 B.C., AR tetradrachm (17.28 gm). Slow quadriga right driven by charioteer crowned by Nike flying left, ketos right in exergue/ΣVRAKO—ΣI—ON, head of Arethusa right surrounded by four dolphins. Boehringer 440 (V233/R316), same dies.

Sicily, Syracuse, Hieron II, 275-216 B.C., AR 16 litra (13.39 gm). Diademed and veiled head of Queen Philistis left/BAΣIΛIΣΣ[AΣ] above, ΦIΛIΣTIΔOΣ in exergue, Nike driving fast quadriga right, ΦI above reins, trident below horses, linear border. Cf. Gulbenkian 355 (without ΦI and trident) and Jameson 878 (slow quadriga without I and trident).

Sicily, Syracuse, Fifth Republic, 214-212 B.C., AR 12 litra (10.11 gm). Head of Athena left wearing crested Corinthian helmet ornamented with snake/ΣYPAKOΣIΩN, Artemis standing left drawing bow, quiver at shoulder, dog running left, ΞA in left field. SNG Copenhagen 878.

Zeugitania, Carthage, circa 213-211 B.C., AR half shekel (4.04 gm). Sicilian mint. Male head right wearing corn wreath/Horse galloping right, Punic letter below, all within laurel wreath. SNG Copenhagen 378. This and the following coin are part of a Barcid issue which must be attributed to Sicily on the basis of hoard evidence. The male figure portrayed is probably Triptolemos, although Hannibal himself has been suggested.
Zeugitania, Carthage, circa 213-211 B.C., AR quarter shekel (1.76 gm). Sicilian mint. Male head right wearing corn wreath/Horse galloping right, Punic letter below. SNG Copenhagen 380.

Kings of Thrace, Lysimachus, 323-281 B.C., AR drachm (4.24 gm). Sestus mint, struck 299/8-297/6. Head of Herakles right wearing lion skin headdress/ΛΥΣΙΜΑΧΟΥ ΒΑΣΙΛΕΩΣ, Zeus enthroned left holding sceptre and eagle, forepart of lion over Ⓐ in left field, cornucopiae below throne. Thompson, "The Mints of Lysimachus," in Essays Robinson, 22.

Macedonia Under the Romans, third century A.D., AE 26mm (12.85 gm). ΑΛΕΞΑΝΔΡΟΥ, head of Herakles right wearing lion skin headdress/ΚΟΙΝΟΝ ΜΑΚΕΔΟΝΩΝ ΟΜΟΝΟΙΑ, turreted female figure seated left, Nike standing right, small figure between. Cf. BMC 98.
Acarnania, Leucas, circa 400-330 B.C., AR stater (8.42 gm). Pegasus right with curved wing, Λ below/Head of Athena right wearing Corinthian helmet, cantharus behind. Cf. BMC 45.
Aetolia, Aetolian League, 279-168 B.C., AR hemidrachm (2.46 gm). Head of Aetolia right wearing petasos/ΑΙΤΩΛΩΝ, Calydonian boar standing right, Σ below, Ⓐ between rear legs. BMC 16-26.
listings.condition: Obverse double struck, otherwise Extremely fine

listings.description: Boeotia, Thebes, 379-338 B.C., AR stater (12.20 gm). Boeotian shield/Volute crater, KP—AT. BMC 157.

Aegina, fourth century B.C., AR stater (11.96 gm). Tortoise/Skew incuse, A in upper left compartment, I in upper right. Cf. Milbank pl. iii, 4 and BMC 184 (both drachms with A—I on obverse in addition).

Mysia, Pergamum, circa 200-133 B.C., AR tetradrachm (12.59 gm). Cista mystica from which serpent emerges, in ivy wreath/Bow case ornamented with aphlaston flanked by two coiled serpents, ΠΕ in left field, symbol in right. Cf. SNG Copenhagen 403ff.

Aeolis, Myrina, circa 160 B.C., AR tetradrachm (16.73 gm). Laureate head of Apollo Grynaeus right/ΜΥΡΙΝΑΙΩΝ, Apollo Grynaeus, nude to waist, walking right, holding filleted laurel branch in left hand and phiale in right, omphalos and amphora at his feet, Ⓐ in left field, all within laurel wreath. SNG Copenhagen 223.
Ionia, Clazomenae, circa 387-300 B.C., AR hemidrachm (1.94 gm). Laureate head of Apollo three-quarters left/ΚΛΑΖΟ ΙΚΕΣΙΟΣ, swan with wings spread standing left. Babelon II, 2001.
listings.condition: Rare. Obverse off center. Very fine

listings.description: Lydia, Sardis, circa 575 B.C., EL trite (4.72 gm). Lion's head right with spiky protuberance on nose and herringbone mane/Double incuse. ACGC 14.
Lydia, Sardis, Croesus, 561-546 B.C., AV stater of the light series (8.04 gm). Forepart of lion right confronting forepart of bull left/Double incuse. SNG von Aulock 2875.
Lydia, Sardis, Time of Croesus and later, circa 550-500 B.C., AR hemistater (4.87 gm). Forepart of lion right confronting forepart of bull left/Double incuse.
Cilicia, Tarsus, Datames, 378-372 B.C., AR stater or double siglos (10.71 gm). Facing head of Arethusa/Datames, head of Ares right in crested helmet. SNG von Aulock 5936.
Phoenicia, Aradus, second century B.C., AR drachm (3.98 gm). Bee, A to left, RE to right/APAΔIΩN, stag standing right before palm tree. SNG Copenhagen 32.
Judaea, First Revolt, 66-70 C.E., AR shekel of Year Two (14.13 gm). Shekel of Israel, chalice, Year Two above/Jerusalem is Holy, stem with three fruit. Meshorer 151.

Judaea, Second Revolt, 132-135 C.E., AR tetradrachm (14.05 gm). Attributed to Year Three (134 C.E.). Shim'on, facade of Temple with Ark of the Covenant, wavy line above, barrier below/For the Freedom of Jerusalem, lulav with etrog on left. Meshorer 201.

Characene, Attambelos I, 44/3-40/39 B.C., AR tetradrachm (15.57 gm). Diademed head of Attambelos I right/BAΣIΛ[EΩΣ] ATTAMBH[ΛOY] ΣΩTHP[OΣ KAI EYEPΓETOY], Herakles seated left holding club, [monogram] in upper left field. SNG Copenhagen 313.

Kushans, Kanishka, circa 130-158 A.D., AV stater (7.91 gm). Legend, king standing left, holding spear, bow slung over shoulder, pointing to altar/Okhsho (Siva) walking left, holding spear, small animal behind, symbol and legend in field. Mitchiner 3064.

Kushans, Vasu Deva, circa 195-230 A.D., AV stater (7.96 gm). Legend, king standing left, holding sceptre and pointing to altar with elephant goad/Okhsho (Siva) standing facing, holding trident and fillet, bull standing left behind, symbol and legend in field. Mitchiner 3387ff.

Ptolemaic Egypt, Ptolemy I Soter, As king, 305-283 B.C., AR tetradrachm (14.33 gm). Diademed head of Ptolemy I right, tiny Δ behind ear/ΠTOΛEMAIOY BAΣIΛEΩΣ, eagle standing left on thunderbolt, P over A in left field. Svoronos 247.

Libya, Revolt of the Libyans, circa 241-238 B.C., AR stater (7.42 gm). Head of young Herakles left in lion skin headdress/ΛIBYΩN in exergue, lion walking right, Punic letter above. Muller 348. SNG Copenhagen 239-242.
Aes grave, Rome, 269-265 B.C., AE uncia (23.16 gm). Knucklebone/Knucklebone. Sydenham 36a.
Umbria, Tuder, circa 235 B.C., AE semis (43.77 gm). Umbrian legend, sleeping dog, ~~ beneath, lyre, ( in field. Haeberlin pl. 81, 11. Vecchi 164.
C. Naevius Balbus, 79 B.C., AR denarius (3.87 gm). Diademed head of Venus right, S C behind/Victory in fast triga right, C NAE BA_B in exergue. Crawford 382/1b. Sydenham 769b.

Cn. Lentulus, 76-75 B.C., AR denarius (3.90 gm). Draped bust of Genius Populi Romani right, sceptre over shoulder, G P R above/Sceptre with wreath, globe and rudder, EX in left field, S C in right, CN LEN Q below. Crawford 393/1a. Sydenham 752.

C. Egnatius, 75 B.C., AR denarius (3.81 gm). Bust of Cupid right, bow and quiver over shoulder, MAX[SVMVS] behind/Two figures standing within distyle temple, XXI in left field, CN N in right, C EGNATIVS CN F below. Crawford 391/2. Sydenham 788.

Kalenus and Cordus, 70 B.C., AR denarius (3.85 gm). Jugate heads of Honos and Virtus right, HO behind, [VIR] before, KAL[ENI] below/Italia standing right, holding cornucopiae, clasping hands with Roma standing left, caduceus and IA in left field, RO in right, CORDI in exergue. Crawford 403.

C. Servilius, 57 B.C., AR denarius (3.84 gm). Head of Flora right, lituus behind, FLORA PRIMVS before/Two soldiers standing facing, CF in right field, C SERVEIL in exergue. Crawford 423/1. Sydenham 890.

L. Marcius Philippus, 56 B.C., AR denarius (3.92 gm). Diademed head of Ancus Marcius right, lituus behind, ANCVS below/Equestrian statue right on aqueduct, PHILIPPVS behind, A Q V A MR in arches. Crawford 425/1. Sydenham 919.

Faustus Cornelius Sulla, 56 B.C., AR denarius (3.64 gm). Diademed and draped bust of Diana right, crescent above, lituus behind, FAVSTVS before/Sulla seated left, Bocchus kneeling before holding olive branch, Jugurtha kneeling behind, FELIX in right field. Crawford 426/1. This famous reverse depicts the surrender of Jugurtha to Sulla by Bocchus. The scene was engraved on Sulla's signet ring, and the composition on the coin is almost certainly copied from that on the ring.

P. Fonteius P. f. Capito, 55 B.C., AR denarius (3.99 gm). Helmeted and draped bust of Mars right, trophy over shoulder, P FONTEIVS P F CAPITO III VIR/Horseman right, warrior and captive below, helmet and shield in right field, MN FON TR MIL. Crawford 429/1.

A. Plautius, 55 B.C., AR denarius (4.18 gm). Turreted head of Cybele right, A PLAVTIVS before, AED CVR SC behind/Kneeling figure before camel right, IVDAEVS before, [BAC]CHIVS in exergue. Crawford 431/1.
Julius Caesar, 49-48 B.C., AR denarius (4.18 gm). Mint moving with Caesar. Pontifical emblems/Elephant right trampling serpent, CAESAR in exergue. Crawford 443/1.

Metellus Scipio and M. Eppius, 47-46 B.C., AR denarius (3.98 gm). Africa mint (Utica?). Laureate head of Africa right wearing lion skin headdress, corn ear and Q METELL before, [SCIP]IO IM[P] behind, plough below/Hercules standing facing resting on club, LEG F C in left field, EPPIVS in right. Crawford 461/1.

Marc Antony and Octavia, 39 B.C., AR cistophorus (11.95 gm). M ANTONIVS IMP COS DESIG ITER ET TERT, head of Antony right wearing ivy wreath, lituus below, all within wreath of ivy and berries/III VIR R P C, cista mystica flanked by two coiled serpents, surmounted by bust of Octavia right. Sydenham 1197.
Tiberius, 14-37 A.D., AV aureus (7.64 gm). TI CAESAR DIVI AVG F AVGVSTVS, laureate head of Tiberius right/PONTIF MAXIM, Livia (as Pax) seated right, holding branch, RIC 3.
Caligula, 37-41 A.D., AE sestertius (28.65 gm). C CAESAR AVG GERMANICVS PON M TR POT, laureate head of Caligula left/S P Q R / P P / OB CIVES / SERVATOS all within oak wreath. RIC 27.

featured_items.title: Cover Coin
featured_items.description: Septimius Severus, 193-211 A.D. Gold aureus (7.16 gm). Rome mint, struck 201-209 A.D. Obverse: SEVERVS PIVS AVG, laureate bust of Septimius Severus right, border of dots. Reverse: VIRTVS AVGVSTORVM, Septimius Severus between Geta and Caracalla, all in military dress, with cloaks flying behind, on horses rearing left, raising right hands in address, border of dots. RIC 305 (pl. 7, 15), same obverse die. BMCRE 374 (pl. 37, 1), same obverse die. Fleur de coin. Septimius Severus gained the purple by sheer force of arms, and therefore he needed to take particular care to establish the legitimacy of his dynasty. One aspect of his consequent publicity campaign was the repeated portrayal of family members on the coins. On this reverse Severus is joined by his sons, and the trio advertise their military success by representing themselves in field attire saluting the troops. The bearded Severus and his older son and joint Augustus Caracalla both appear laureate, while Geta, who bore only the rank of Caesar before 209, remains bare-headed. Although carefully individualized, the three are portrayed as a unified force on horses rearing in unison. Despite Severus' careful dynastic plans, this facade of family unity did not long outlast his death.
